channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Expert Recalls Data on Kazakhstan's Territory Transfer to Uzbekistan in 1956
item.description: Expert Eldar Konayev highlighted that in 1956, a portion of Kazakhstan's territory, including the Bostandyk district, was transferred to Uzbekistan. He noted that politician Zhumabek Tashenov led the initiative group that proposed this transfer.

item.title: Appeals Court in Tashkent Replaces Suspended Sentences with Real Prison Terms for Blogger Kokow and Actress Barchin Gafurova
item.description: An appellate court in Tashkent has replaced suspended sentences with real prison terms for blogger Kokow, actress Barchin Gafurova, and a third woman. They were found guilty of extortion and insult, receiving sentences ranging from 3.5 to 4.5 years.

item.title: France Agrees to Receive Taliban Diplomats for Migration Talks
item.description: France has agreed to host Taliban diplomats for discussions on Afghan migrant returns, a source confirmed. French officials state these talks do not signify diplomatic recognition of the Taliban regime. The discussions aim to facilitate the return of Afghan nationals in France deemed security threats.

item.title: IOM Records Over 95,000 Border Movements Into Afghanistan in Two Weeks
item.description: The International Organization for Migration (IOM) recorded 95,489 movements into Afghanistan between October 25 and November 7. The majority, 68%, were from Iran, and 32% from Pakistan. During the same period, 44,899 movements out of Afghanistan were recorded, primarily towards Iran and Pakistan.

item.title: Chronic Sleep Deprivation Increases Risk of Heart Attack and Stroke, Doctor Warns
item.description: According to somnologist Ilya Smirnov, consistently insufficient sleep accelerates atherosclerosis, significantly raising the risk of vascular diseases like heart attack and stroke. He highlighted obstructive sleep apnea as particularly dangerous, especially when combined with excess weight, leading to oxygen deprivation and stress hormone release.

item.title: NATO Cancels Planned 2027 Leaders Summit in Albania, Reduces Ministerial Meetings
item.description: NATO has decided not to hold its planned leaders' summit in Albania in 2027, though a summit in 2028 is not ruled out. The alliance is also reducing the number of defense and foreign affairs ministerial meetings. NATO states summits are held when necessary, not annually.

item.title: Bahrain Issues Security Warnings Amid Escalating Iran-US Tensions in Gulf
item.description: Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued security warnings, urging residents to seek safety amid rising tensions between Iran and the United States in the Gulf. The alerts, posted on X, followed claims by Iran's IRGC of targeting a US radar installation. Bahrain hosts the US Navy's Fifth Fleet headquarters.

item.title: UK Special Envoy Discusses Easing Taliban-Pakistan Tensions
item.description: UK Special Representative for Afghanistan Richard Lindsay is engaging in talks to ease tensions and normalize relations between the Taliban and Pakistan. Lindsay plans to visit Pakistan for further discussions with officials. The Taliban expressed appreciation for UK's humanitarian aid and efforts towards regional peace.

item.title: Israeli intelligence: Iran plans assassination attempt on Trump
item.description: Israeli intelligence agency Mossad has reportedly shared information with the CIA indicating Iran may be planning an assassination attempt on U.S. President Donald Trump and other high-ranking American officials. The report, citing sources, suggests Iran might use attack drones as part of the plot. This follows previous warnings and skepticism from U.S. intelligence.

item.title: Central Asian Fathers Embrace Active Roles Beyond Traditional Breadwinning
item.description: Fathers in Kyrgyzstan, Uzbekistan, and Tajikistan are increasingly involved in their children's daily lives, moving beyond the traditional role of sole provider. Stories highlight fathers reading, helping with homework, and discussing feelings, fostering closer bonds.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Expand Free Medications List Starting 2027
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to increase the range of free medications provided to the public starting in 2027. An electronic policy will be introduced via the Single Interactive State Services portal, detailing each citizen's status, available free medical services, and medication list.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Prosecutor General Orders Probe into Yandex Service Failures and Data Leaks
item.description: Kazakhstan's Prosecutor General has ordered a comprehensive review of the Information Security Committee's activities and an investigation into failures within Yandex services. This action follows concerns about the public disclosure of Kazakh citizens' personal data. The probe aims to ensure compliance with constitutional rights protecting personal data.

item.title: Yemeni Government Seeks International Aid to Recapture Bab el-Mandeb Strait from Houthis
item.description: The official Yemeni government has appealed to the international community for assistance in retaking the Bab el-Mandeb Strait from Houthi control. This strategic waterway is crucial for global shipping and has been a point of contention in the ongoing conflict.

item.title: Uzbekistan and ACWA to Explore Carbon Credit Generation at Wind Farms
item.description: Uzbekistan and ACWA have signed a memorandum of cooperation on carbon markets and international greenhouse gas reduction mechanisms. The agreement focuses on exploring the inclusion of ACWA's wind power projects in Uzbekistan into international carbon market mechanisms under the Paris Agreement, including carbon credit generation.

item.title: Twelve Former Colony Staff Convicted in Atbasar Torture Case After Third Trial Attempt
item.description: Twelve former employees of the Atbasar colony have been sentenced to two years of restricted freedom in a case involving the alleged beating of dozens of inmates. The court reached a conviction on its third attempt, replacing the initial charge of torture with abuse of power. The verdict was delivered on November 13.

item.title: Pakistan Minister to Visit India for SCO Forum Amid Strained Relations
item.description: Pakistan's Climate Change Minister, Musadik Masood Malik, will travel to New Delhi for a Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) forum from November 20-22. This marks the first visit by a Pakistani federal minister to India in over three years, following a military confrontation in May 2025. The forum aims to discuss civilisational dialogue and cultural understanding.

item.title: Two Oil Tankers Hit Mines and Catch Fire in Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Two oil tankers attempting to transit the Strait of Hormuz struck naval mines, resulting in explosions and fires aboard both vessels. Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) reported the incident, stating the tankers were engaged in illegal cargo transport. The ships were reportedly using an unauthorized route with navigation systems disabled.

item.title: Global Oil Prices Decline for Second Consecutive Week Amid Market Concerns
item.description: Global oil prices, including Brent and WTI, have fallen for the second consecutive week, with both benchmarks decreasing by approximately 2.5%. This decline is attributed to increased supply and weakening global demand, further influenced by a report from the International Energy Agency. US inventory data also contributed to the price drop.

item.title: Aktobe-Kandyagash Highway Section Now Toll Road
item.description: A section of the Aktobe-Kandyagash highway in Kazakhstan became a toll road on November 15. This 89-kilometer stretch is now integrated into the Kandyagash-Makat toll road, increasing its total length to 469.5 km. While some parts are free for cars, other sections require payment for all vehicle types. Discounts are available for vehicles registered in nearby areas.

item.title: Migration from Afghanistan viewed as a silent referendum on Taliban rule
item.description: Mass migration from Afghanistan since the Taliban's return is driven by poverty, unemployment, and hardships, but also by political and social restrictions. For many, leaving signifies a rejection of curtailed freedoms and future prospects. This departure acts as a silent referendum on the quality of Taliban governance, reflecting citizens' confidence in the country's future.

item.title: Kazakhstan considers increasing mobile transfer limit to 2 million tenge
item.description: Kazakhstan is considering raising the limit for mobile transfers per operation from 1 million to 2 million tenge. This change would apply only to interbank mobile payments between individuals via phone number. The National Bank has not specified a concrete implementation date, noting the project is still under inter-agency approval. QR code payments are unaffected.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan must live in unity, with each citizen contributing to national development
item.description: Every citizen of Kyrgyzstan must contribute to the nation's development while living in harmony and unity, stated public figure Aikökül Myrzakarimova. She emphasized President Sadyr Japarov's call to preserve peace and inter-ethnic accord, noting Kyrgyzstan's progress and aspirations to become a recognized global power. She urged against divisive actions.

item.title: Iran Claims Drone Attack on US Air Defence Radar in Bahrain
item.description: Iran's Revolutionary Guard claimed to have targeted a US air defence radar installation in Bahrain with six drones, calling it retaliation for US actions. Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued security warnings. US Central Command rejected a previous similar claim by Iran. Details on damage or casualties were not provided.

item.title: Zelensky: US Offered NATO Membership for Ukraine in Exchange for Donbas Concessions
item.description: Ukrainian President Zelensky stated that the US proposed Ukraine join NATO in exchange for concessions on Donbas. He indicated a willingness to hold a referendum on the issue if security guarantees are provided and funds allocated for reconstruction.

item.title: Two Underground Call Centers Shut Down in Tashkent, 72 Arrested in Crypto Fraud Scheme
item.description: Authorities in Tashkent have shut down two illegal call centers involved in financial fraud and cryptocurrency schemes. Seventy-two individuals were arrested, and a total of $576,000 in crypto assets were seized. The centers were engaged in illicit money transfers for online casinos and defrauding men online.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Establish Special Kindergartens for Children of Incarcerated Mothers
item.description: Uzbekistan will establish special state preschool educational organizations named 'Mother and Child Centers' for children up to three years old. These centers will be based at correctional facilities and will operate as state educational institutions under the Ministry of Preschool and School Education. They will provide round-the-clock care for up to five children per group.

item.title: Saudi Arabia Intercepts Houthi Missiles and Drones Targeting Riyadh and Eastern Province
item.description: Saudi air defenses intercepted two ballistic missiles launched by Yemen's Houthi movement towards the capital, Riyadh. The coalition also reported intercepting three drones over the Eastern Province, a key region for the kingdom's oil and gas reserves. These attacks follow recent drone strikes on Riyadh and southern Saudi Arabia.

item.title: UN Reports Surge in Afghan Poppy Cultivation; Russia Disputes Findings
item.description: The UN Office on Drugs and Crime reports a 330% increase in poppy cultivation in Afghanistan, reaching over 43,000 hectares, with opium production up 400% to about 1,500 tonnes. Russia has called the UN report "unbalanced" and "custom-made political propaganda," supporting the Taliban's denial of the findings.

item.title: Afghan Traders Face Significant Losses Due to Delays on Iran's Rimdan Route
item.description: Afghan traders report lengthy delays, up to a month, on Iran's Rimdan route for fruit and vegetable exports. This causes produce to spoil, leading to substantial financial losses. Iranian officials reportedly prioritize their own fuel trucks, exacerbating congestion and spoilage.

item.title: Zelenskiy: US Floated Idea of Ukraine Ceding Donbas for NATO Membership
item.description: President Zelenskiy stated that US negotiators proposed Ukraine cede the Donbas region in exchange for NATO membership. He reiterated Kyiv's stance against territorial concessions but indicated a potential referendum if security guarantees and military support were provided.

item.title: Kazakhstan Ministry Warns Against Scams Involving SIM Cards and WhatsApp Accounts
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Internal Affairs warns citizens against scams where fraudsters ask minors to register SIM cards and WhatsApp accounts in their names, promising payment. These accounts can be used for criminal activities, and those who register them may face legal consequences.

item.title: Guatemala Declares State of Emergency After Lawmaker and Police Officers Murdered
item.description: Guatemala has declared a 30-day state of emergency in two eastern departments due to a wave of armed attacks, including the murder of a lawmaker and three police officers. The special regime grants security forces additional powers, including restrictions on public gatherings and warrantless arrests.

item.title: Uzbek Student Sentenced to Over a Year in Prison in South Korea for Terrorism Financing
item.description: An Uzbek student in South Korea has been sentenced to one year and four months in prison for transferring funds to an extremist group in Syria. In addition to the prison term, the student was ordered to pay 1.25 million won.

item.title: New US Ambassador to Kyrgyzstan, Stephen Gillen, Assumes Diplomatic Duties
item.description: Stephen Gillen has officially begun his diplomatic service as the new U.S. Ambassador to Kyrgyzstan. Having taken the oath of office in Bishkek, Gillen brings extensive experience in national security and crisis diplomacy. His appointment aims to strengthen the strategic partnership between the United States and Kyrgyzstan during his tenure.

item.title: Tashkent Reports 307 New HIV Cases in 9 Months, Meningococcal Infections Surge
item.description: Tashkent has recorded 307 new HIV cases in the first nine months of 2026, bringing the total number of people living with HIV to 10,382. Meningococcal infections have also seen a significant rise, increasing 35-fold to 354 cases. Several other infectious diseases also showed an increase compared to the previous year.

item.title: Pakistan Military Reports Killing 24 Militants, Including Two Afghans, in Counterterrorism Operations
item.description: Pakistan's military announced that security forces killed 24 militants, including two Afghan nationals, during counterterrorism operations in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan. Four Pakistani security personnel were also killed. The military identified the Afghan nationals as members of the banned Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP).

item.title: US Diesel Prices Fall Below $6 Per Gallon for First Time in Two Months
item.description: Diesel fuel prices in the United States have dropped below $6 per gallon for the first time in two months, according to Reuters. This decrease is attributed to falling oil prices and weakening demand. Brent crude oil has lost 18.5% of its value in the past two weeks.

item.title: Afghan and Iranian Ministers Discuss Agricultural Exports and Trade Facilitation
item.description: Afghanistan's Finance Minister met with Iran's Agriculture Minister to boost bilateral economic cooperation. Discussions focused on preparing for the joint economic commission meeting, expanding Afghan agricultural exports to Iran, and ensuring 24-hour customs operations. Both sides also addressed challenges for Afghan traders and preventing smuggling.

item.title: Kazakh Court Delivers Guilty Verdict in Torture Case After Two Acquittals
item.description: A Kazakh court has issued a third verdict against 12 former prison employees accused of torturing inmates. Initially acquitted twice, the employees were found guilty of exceeding their authority, receiving two-year sentences with restrictions. Nine received a reduced one-year sentence and were released on bail. Compensation for moral damages will be awarded to some victims.

item.title: Businessman Seizes Kabul Land Amid Allegations of Taliban Collusion
item.description: Kabul residents report a businessman from Khost province has seized approximately 200 residential plots in Kabul New City, claiming ownership of 20 hectares. This occurred after a Taliban commission declared legal issues resolved and land transactions resumed. Residents question how the Taliban allowed this seizure after officially approving the area's development plan.
